items.title: Al Grey interviewed by Michael Woods, Scottsdale, Arizona, March 3, 1995
items.q: until when we’d go out where we’d have Frank Sinatra and Ella Fitzgerald, that meant that Count Basie’s band didn’t have no chance to play... here you have all these great musicians sitting there playing the music for the singers

ctx.x: Now what was that first year you started with Basie?

57. 1957. And so I go into the band, went to Washington DC, came back, went to New York for a recording. And this is the first recordings that Neal Hefti brought to the band. And this is when we recorded, I got my first solo in the band, “Little Tempo Please” and then after a couple of days, we went to England. And we went to England to play for the Queen, which is where we played a Royal Command Performance for the Queen of England. Yeah, that’s it, that is the one. This is when I joined the band, and this man…

the Kansas City Seven, see, which I had chances and all like that to play later on for a movie with the Kansas City Seven with Count Basie for a film made in Paris with Ann Margaret. But all before that, we had many nights that it wouldn’t be that many people in the place because they were automatically looking for that singer. And if you don’t have that singer, that means something different then. And now coming along, but we had such great soloists, that the band could make it by this change, with “Whirly Bird”…
